reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes Forsage X-Gold as an income-generating opportunity, soliciting a $10 entry slot while claiming it can produce a $322 cash return through a tiered structure. The speaker also encourages buying multiple slots and claims repeated wallet income and rapid money multiplication, linking payment to unusually large returns. The presentation associates additional income with building a team and shows a branching structure, though it does not establish that any payment or profit was received.

The first slot of X gold is worth 10$
There are 2 positions under this
So you will get 322$ cash from here
the slot you buy once in your life That will keep giving you money again and again

opening.argument: Judge the speaker's technical claims as claims, not proof that the program works. He asks viewers to study the design, and the presentation supplies a structure they can examine. His statements that the contracts are audited and verified are assertions in the video; the video does not independently establish an audit or a realized return. That gap matters when deciding whether an explanation of a proposed system should itself be treated as a demonstrated deception.

citations.quote: just get connected to the systems and understand its power and study this design project
It's 100% decentralized smart contract Audited and verified smart contracts.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The $10 slot and $322 figure cited by the other side establish what the speaker says the structure can pay, not that a viewer paid or received that amount. Likewise, the repeated-income language is a claim about the proposed mechanism, not evidence of an actual payout. The distinction is especially important where the speaker presents the positions as a diagram for viewers to understand.

citations.quote: The first slot of X gold is worth 10$
So you will get 322$ cash from here

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An invitation to study the design is not a risk warning. The speaker urges viewers to join and buy a slot, while promising rapid multiplication of their money. No completed payment needs to appear on screen for the video to promote the income scheme.

citations.quote: Join hands with us
then buy the slot You can do your money here 10 times in few days

opening.argument: The central presentation is a worked explanation of how X-Gold's positions and slots are supposed to operate. The speaker explicitly says he will explain the system, walks from two positions to four, eight and sixteen, and draws a branching diagram on a whiteboard. A judge can recognize that instructional format without treating the diagram as proof that anyone earned the amounts discussed.

citations.quote: now I will tell you how X gold works
you get two positions in below this Then you'll get 4 positions below 4 you the 8 position and below 8 you will get 16 positions

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing statement emphasizes the entry price and projected cash return but leaves out how much of the presentation is spent explaining the arrangement of positions. The quoted $322 is described as coming from that structure; the whiteboard illustrates a calculation, not a recorded transaction. The evidence supports an instructional reading even if the speaker is enthusiastic about the program.

citations.quote: So you will get 322$ cash from here

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Explaining the mechanics does not make the video neutral. The speaker connects purchased slots to repeated income, tells viewers to buy, and urges them to upgrade their teams. The diagram helps communicate the very tiered income opportunity being promoted.

citations.quote: the slot you buy once in your life That will keep giving you money again and again
Friends, do yes to this program, you should also upgrade your team

opening.argument: The speaker describes priced slots and successive levels, which can be read as the terms of a program being presented for purchase. His reference to team activity does not, by itself, specify a commission paid for recruiting a person. Nor do the sampled frames show a checkout, wallet address or payment request: they show a presenter and whiteboard calculations. The record establishes a sales-oriented explanation with ambitious income claims, but it does not show an actual transfer or identify a recruitment commission.

citations.quote: The second level of this is the slot of $ 20
Your team will also follow you here, till the 15th level you will be followed

rebuttal.rebuttal: A branching diagram and a $10 starting price do not alone establish the source of each payout. The other side cites a projected $322 return, but the cited passage does not identify a commission for signing up a new person. Those omissions limit what can be concluded about the payment mechanism, even while the income claims deserve scrutiny.

citations.quote: The first slot of X gold is worth 10$
So you will get 322$ cash from here

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A checkout screen or completed transfer is not required to assess what this video promotes. The speaker tells viewers to buy slots, describes people joining their structures, and says positions will generate wallet income. The defense's narrower point about an explicitly named recruitment commission does not explain away that combined pitch.
